title: Credit Policy Standard on the Number of Auto Loans One Borrower May Carry
content:
A customer may carry several Auto Loans at Piedmont Crescent Bank. Two counts bound how many, and a third condition closes the door entirely.

## 1. The standard

1.1 The count of the customer's Auto Loans in applied, active or delinquent status must be below 3 before a new application is recorded.

1.2 The count of the customer's loans of the requested product in applied, active or delinquent status must be below the number of loans of that product one customer may hold, as that product publishes it.

1.3 A customer with any auto loan in charged-off status cannot apply.

1.4 Loans that are paid off and applications that were withdrawn do not count toward either count.

## 2. The evidence both counts rest on

Both counts are read from the bank's own record of the customer's loans, and are taken before the new application is recorded. The loans counted are those held by the applicant. What the customer says about how many loans they hold does not settle either count; the record does.

## 3. The counts side by side

| Customer's record | Count of Auto Loans in applied, active or delinquent status | Count of those on the requested product | Charged-off loan on file | Application may be recorded |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Two active loans of another product, none of the requested product | 2 | 0 | no | yes, both counts are below their limits |
| Three active loans across products | 3 | any | no | no, the first count is not below 3 |
| One active loan, one paid off, one withdrawn | 1 | as counted | no | yes, the paid-off and withdrawn loans do not count |
| Two active loans, one of them charged off at an earlier date | as counted | as counted | yes | no, a charged-off loan on file closes the door |

## 4. How the first count is read

The first count is a limit of 3 on the whole of a customer's Auto Loans holding, not a limit per product. A customer holding two loans of one product and one of another has a count of 3 and is therefore not below the limit, whatever the second count reads.
